audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4..6].side read Yasuo while win[4..6] read Anivia; the packet chart agrees with win[].
audit.why: The lane flips at Glacial Storm — phases[4].why itself says 'Yasuo must respect every stun line now' while the side said Yasuo.

Yasuo spikes at level 6 (Last Breath 70s at rank 1) and at two crit items; Anivia spikes at Lost Chapter, 6, and Rylai's/Seraph's. Last Breath needs an airborne target, which he supplies himself with a 2-stack Steel Tempest.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now states the knock-up requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly claims Wind Wall blocks more than it does: tldr/report[0] say it 'blocks your Q and E', and wants.foe[1] says it blocks 'Flash Frost or R'. Frostbite is a targeted spell and Glacial Storm is a persistent zone — neither is a projectile.
audit.why: Riot text: Wind Wall 'creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', 400 range, 25/23/21/19/17s. The kit flags projectile on Anivia's Q only; E and R carry no projectile flag.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall stops Flash Frost and nothing else — keep farming him with the 4s Frostbite while the wall is up, and save the stun for its downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers and two lines of filler about Anivia's own W and R.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 for 4s of cover; Sweeping Blade is on a 0.5s cooldown so it is effectively always available and only terrain stops it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both numbers and the Crystallize counter.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentioned Way of the Wanderer's moving shield absorbing the front of your burst, or that each Sweeping Blade builds a Gathering Storm stack toward the knock-up.
audit.why: Both are in Riot's text and both change when you commit.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Crystallize for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1 for 4s of cover — it stops Flash Frost only, so chip with the 4s Frostbite while it stands and save the stun for its downtime. - Sweeping Blade is never on cooldown; Crystallize is what actually stops it.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by making him dash first — Crystallize cuts Sweeping Blade off from the wave and the stun lands on a Yasuo with no exit.

edits.before: Yasuo whiffs Wind Wall and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Wind Wall is 400 wide — storm behind it and it stops nothing.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: A blocked Flash Frost costs 80 mana and your only CC.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Every dash feeds Gathering Storm — at two stacks the next Steel Tempest knocks you airborne.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Yasuo walks straight at you.
edits.after: His minions are free dash targets and the Flow shield charges while he moves — fight him where he has neither.

edits.before: Level 6: Last Breath threatens a burst kill on Anivia's egg, though Glacial Storm finally starts narrowing the gap, making this a tense but still Yasuo-favored spike.
edits.after: Level 6: Last Breath needs his own Steel Tempest knock-up first, and it bursts the egg — though Glacial Storm finally starts narrowing the gap for you here.

edits.before: Hold Wind Wall to block Flash Frost or R and negate Anivia's whole combo
edits.after: Hold Wind Wall for Flash Frost — the stun is the only piece it stops

notes: Main correction: the page told the reader Wind Wall blocks Anivia's E and R. It does not — Frostbite is targeted and Glacial Storm is a zone; only Flash Frost carries the projectile flag. That single error changes how the entire lane is played, so tldr, winCon, their two report mirrors and wants.foe[1] were all fixed together. Packet suspectName 'His Last Breath' is a false positive — Last Breath is the real R name. Level chart squared to the packet on rows 5-7.
